import.title: Import tasks
import.replaceWarning: The import will replace all current tasks ({{count}}). The project name and calendar stay. You can undo the import with Undo (Ctrl+Z).
import.errorsIntro_one: The file cannot be imported – it contains {{count}} error:
import.errorsIntro_other: The file cannot be imported – it contains {{count}} errors:
import.nothingChanged: Fix the file (e.g. in Excel) and import it again. Nothing in the project has changed.
import.nothingChangedPlan: Save the file again in the original program and import it again. Nothing in the project has changed.

error.tooLarge: The file is too large (over 5 MB). Nothing has changed.
error.unreadable: The file cannot be read – it is damaged or not an Excel / CSV table. Nothing has changed.
error.unsafeXlsx: The file grows suspiciously when unpacked (more than 50 MB or unusual compression). It was not loaded for security reasons. Nothing has changed.
error.unsupported: Only .xlsx and .csv files can be imported. Nothing has changed.
error.empty: The table contains no tasks (the first row must be a header with a Name column).
error.missingName: The first row (table header) has no “Name” column.
error.tooManyRows: The table has more than 5,000 rows – the app cannot handle that many tasks.
error.invalid: The table data did not pass the check.
error.nameTooLong: the name is longer than 200 characters.
error.notesTooLong: the note is longer than 5,000 characters.
error.badLevel: invalid level (a whole number 1–6, at most 1 more than the previous row).
error.badDuration: the duration must be a whole number of days (0–10,000).
error.badPercent: % complete must be a whole number 0–100.
error.badDate: invalid “Start no earlier than” date (use e.g. 2026-11-18).
error.badNumber: the row number (No.) must be a positive whole number.
error.duplicateNumber: another row already has the same row number (No.).
error.unknownPredecessor: a predecessor refers to a row number that is not in the table.
error.selfDependency: a task cannot be its own predecessor.
error.phaseDependency: a phase cannot have a link (nor be a predecessor).
error.parentNotPhase: sub-items can only be under a phase (check the Level and Type columns).
error.cycle: the links form a loop (the task waits for itself through other tasks).

msp.invalidXml: The file is not valid XML. Save the plan in MS Project again via File → Save as → XML.
msp.notMsProject: The file is not an MS Project plan (the task list is missing). For GanttProject, use “Plan from GanttProject (.gan)”.
msp.tooMany: The file has more than 5,000 tasks.
msp.tooDeep: Task no. {{row}} is nested deeper than 6 levels (the app cannot handle more).
msp.cycle: The dependencies in the file form a cycle – tasks wait for each other.
msp.invalid: The plan from the file did not pass the app check.

gan.invalidXml: The file is not valid XML. Save the plan in GanttProject again.
gan.notGanttProject: The file is not a GanttProject plan (the task list is missing). For MS Project, use “Plan from MS Project (XML)”.
gan.tooMany: The file has more than 5,000 tasks.
gan.tooDeep: Task no. {{row}} is nested deeper than 6 levels (the app cannot handle more).
gan.cycle: The dependencies in the file form a cycle – tasks wait for each other.
gan.invalid: The plan from the file did not pass the app check.

project.costHint: Total cost of all tasks and phases in the project

table.caption: Project task list
table.collapseHint: Hide the tasks of this phase (in the table and the chart)
table.expandHint: Show the tasks of this phase
table.confirmDeleteWithChildren_one: Really delete phase “{{name}}” including {{count}} item inside it? You can undo this with Undo (Ctrl+Z).
table.confirmDeleteWithChildren_other: Really delete phase “{{name}}” including {{count}} items inside it? You can undo this with Undo (Ctrl+Z).
table.startHint: Start. If you change it, the task starts no earlier than this date (📌 – same as moving the bar). Clear the date to remove the constraint.
table.finishHint: Finish = last working day. If you change it, the duration in working days is recalculated.
table.milestoneFinishHint: A milestone lasts 0 days – its finish equals its start. Move the start instead.
table.invalidDate: That is not a valid date – the previous value was restored.
table.finishBeforeStart: The finish cannot be before the start ({{start}}). The previous value was restored.
table.constraint: Starts no earlier than {{date}} (set by moving the bar or in the table). Click to remove the constraint – Ctrl+Z undoes it.
table.constraintIgnored: Starts no earlier than {{date}} – but right now a dependency on a predecessor only allows a later start. Click to remove the constraint.
table.constraintClear: Remove the “start no earlier than {{date}}” constraint from task {{name}}
table.resizeHint: Drag to change the column width. Double-click = default width. From the keyboard: arrows ←/→ (with Shift in bigger steps), Home = default.
table.dragHint: Drag the row elsewhere. Over a phase: top part = before it, middle = into it, bottom part = after it. Esc cancels.
table.kindLockedHint: This phase contains tasks, so it must stay a phase. To change it, move its tasks out first.
table.wbsHint: Number in the project breakdown (WBS – Work Breakdown Structure). E.g. 2.3 = third item of the second phase. Predecessors are written with row numbers from the No. column.
table.name: Name
table.durationHint: Number of working days. A milestone has duration 0.
table.datesHint: Calculated automatically from duration, predecessors and the calendar. Finish = last working day.
table.phaseDatesHint: A phase runs from the start of its first task to the finish of its last task – calculated automatically.
table.phaseDurationHint: Number of working days from the start to the finish of the phase. Calculated from its tasks.
table.predecessorsHint: Row numbers this task follows. E.g. 2; 5+3 = after the finish of row 2 and 3 working days after the finish of row 5. Dependency type after the number: FS (default, not written) = starts after finish, SS = starts with start, FF = finishes with finish, SF = finishes before start – e.g. 3SS+2.
table.phasePredecessorsHint: A phase cannot have predecessors yet.
table.cycleHint: Dates cannot be calculated: the links form a loop (the task waits for itself). Fix the predecessors.
table.confirmDelete: Really delete “{{name}}”? You can undo this with Undo (Ctrl+Z).
table.emptyText: Not sure how to start? The wizard guides you through the name, start date, calendar and first phases. Or start from a template, with your first task right away, or have a look at the sample project.
table.invalidName: The name cannot be empty – the original value was restored.
table.confirmDeleteMany_one: Really delete {{count}} item (the selected rows including items in selected phases)? You can undo this with Undo (Ctrl+Z).
table.confirmDeleteMany_other: Really delete {{count}} items (the selected rows including items in selected phases)? You can undo this with Undo (Ctrl+Z).
table.costHint: Cost of the item from the resources and costs in the Task detail panel; for a phase including its sub-items. Hover to see the breakdown.
table.confirmMilestoneLines_one: A milestone may only have a one-off cost and material. {{count}} resource line will be removed. Continue? (Ctrl+Z undoes it.)
table.confirmMilestoneLines_other: A milestone may only have a one-off cost and material. {{count}} resource lines will be removed. Continue? (Ctrl+Z undoes it.)
table.slackHint: Total slack in working days: how much the item may slip without moving the project finish. 0 = critical path (yellow).
table.slackCell: Total slack {{total}} working days (project finish does not move); free slack {{free}} working days (no successor moves either).
table.percentComputed: A phase's % complete is calculated from its tasks – weighted by planned cost from the baseline, otherwise by duration. Enter it on the tasks.
table.milestoneDoneHint: A milestone is either achieved (100 %) or not (0 %)

kind.taskHint: Work that takes a certain number of days.
kind.phaseHint: A group of tasks (a project stage).
kind.milestoneHint: An important moment with no duration, e.g. signing a contract.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.intro: Shortcuts work with the selected row (click into it). On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl.

items.save: Save the project to a file
items.saveAs: Save the project to a new file
items.open: Open a project from a file
items.addTask: New task below the selected row
items.duplicate: Duplicate the selected rows (phases including their tasks)
items.delete: Delete the selected rows (outside a text field – in a field Ctrl+Delete deletes a word)
items.indent: Indent – put under the row above (into a phase)
items.outdent: Outdent – move one level up, after the end of the phase
items.undo: Undo the last change (outside a text field; in a field it undoes typing)
items.confirm: Confirm the edit of a field
items.cancel: Cancel the edit of a field or a drag; outside a field, clear a multiple selection
items.nextField: Go to the next field (Shift+Tab to the previous one)
items.print: Print / save the Gantt chart as PDF

mouseItems.dragBar: Drag a bar in the chart = move the task (sets “start no earlier than” 📌).
mouseItems.dragEdge: Drag the edge of a bar = change the start or finish (duration).
mouseItems.createByDrag: Drag horizontally in the empty strip below the plan = new task with this start (📌) and duration; Esc cancels.
mouseItems.dragRow: Drag a row by ⠿ = move it elsewhere or into a phase.
mouseItems.resizeColumn: Drag the right edge of a column header = change its width; double-click = default width.
mouseItems.drawLink: Drag from the circle at the start / finish of a bar onto another task = draw a dependency (type FS, SS, FF, SF depending on where from and where to).
mouseItems.pin: Click 📌 = remove the “start no earlier than” constraint.
mouseItems.collapse: Click ▾ / ▸ = collapse or expand a phase.
mouseItems.zoom: Ctrl + mouse wheel or spreading / pinching two fingers on the touchpad over the chart = more / less detailed timeline (the day under the pointer stays in place).
mouseItems.multiSelect: Ctrl + click a row or bar = add it to / remove it from the selection; Shift + click = select a continuous range. On a touch screen: hold your finger for ½ s = add / remove. Buttons, shortcuts and dragging then work with all selected rows.
mouseItems.dragGroup: Drag one of the selected bars = move all selected by the same number of working days; drag ⠿ of a selected row = move the whole selection.
mouseItems.resourceTabs: Resources: drag a tab (Professions, Workers…) = change the tab order; on the selected tab the same with Alt+Shift+← / →.
mouseItems.rate: Resources: click an hourly rate (✎) = set it manually, by calculation or from the profession.
mouseItems.detailPanel: Task detail (below the plan): click a task = show its resources and costs; drag the separator above the panel (or ↑ ↓) = change the height; ▾ = collapse.
mouseItems.critical: The Critical path button highlights tasks without slack in yellow; the Slack column shows how many working days a task may slip
mouseItems.absence: Resources → Workers → Absence column: holidays, sick leave, training (affects load, not dates)
mouseItems.load: Load view: click a resource for its histogram and tasks; click a task to open it in the plan
mouseItems.mindMap: In the Map view: Tab = new child node, Enter = new sibling, F2 or typing = rename, Delete = delete, arrows = move, Space = collapse / expand, Alt+Shift+↑/↓ = order; drag a node to move it under another node or between siblings (Esc cancels); the mouse wheel zooms, dragging the background pans the map.

structure.indentHint: Put the selected rows under the row above them (into a phase) – Alt+Shift+→
structure.outdentHint: Move the selected rows one level up, after the end of their phase – Alt+Shift+←
structure.moveUpHint: Move the selected rows (with their tasks) up – Alt+Shift+↑
structure.moveDownHint: Move the selected rows (with their tasks) down – Alt+Shift+↓
structure.noSelection: First click into the row you want to work with.
structure.confirmConvert_one: Row “{{name}}” will become a phase so it can contain tasks. Phases cannot have dependencies yet, so {{count}} dependency will be removed. Continue? (Ctrl+Z undoes it.)
structure.confirmConvert_other: Row “{{name}}” will become a phase so it can contain tasks. Phases cannot have dependencies yet, so {{count}} dependencies will be removed. Continue? (Ctrl+Z undoes it.)

error.notFound: The selected row no longer exists. Click into another row.
error.noPreviousSibling: There is nothing above this row on the same level. It cannot be indented or moved up.
error.noNextSibling: There is nothing below this row on the same level. Move it to another phase by outdenting or dragging.
error.topLevel: The row is already at the top level.
error.maxDepth: A plan can have at most {{max}} levels. The row cannot go any deeper.
error.targetNotPhase: A row can only be placed inside a phase.
error.intoOwnSubtree: A phase cannot be moved into itself or into its own tasks.

structure.selectedHint: Ctrl+click adds or removes a row, Shift+click selects a range, Esc clears the selection
structure.confirmConvertMany_one: Rows above the selection will become phases so they can contain tasks. Phases cannot have dependencies yet, so {{count}} dependency will be removed. Continue? (Ctrl+Z undoes it.)

gantt.chartLabel: Gantt chart – timeline of the tasks. The same data is in the table on the left.
gantt.splitterHint: Drag with the mouse, or use the left/right arrow keys
gantt.zoomHint: How much detail of time to show in the chart. Over the chart you can also use Ctrl + mouse wheel or two fingers on the touchpad.
gantt.dragTaskHint: Drag the bar to move it, its edges to change the start or finish, the circle next to the bar for a new dependency. Esc cancels.
gantt.linkHandle: Drag onto another task to create a dependency. Left half of the target = to its start, right half = to its finish.

linkInvalid.phaseSuccessor: A phase cannot have predecessors yet
linkInvalid.cycle: This would create a loop – the task would wait for itself

gantt.dragMilestoneHint: Drag the milestone to move it. Esc cancels.
gantt.phaseNotDraggable: A phase is calculated from its tasks – move or change its tasks instead.
gantt.constraintOverridden: “{{name}}” cannot start earlier than its predecessors allow (dependency). The “start no earlier than” date was saved, but the dependency wins. To move it earlier, change its predecessors.
gantt.constraintOverriddenMany_one: For {{count}} moved task a dependency applies, so it starts later than where you moved it. The constraint was saved (📌).
gantt.constraintOverriddenMany_other: For {{count}} moved tasks a dependency applies, so they start later than where you moved them. The constraints were saved (📌).
gantt.criticalHint: Highlight the critical path: yellow tasks must not slip, otherwise the project finish moves. The grey bar after a bar shows its slack.
gantt.slackBar_one: Slack {{count}} working day – the task may slip this much without moving the project finish
gantt.slackBar_other: Slack {{count}} working days – the task may slip this much without moving the project finish
gantt.baselineHint: Show the dates of baseline "{{name}}" (saved original plan) in grey under the bars – you see at once what has moved
gantt.baselineNone: No baseline (saved original plan) yet. You save one in the Tracking view.

predecessorError.syntax: “{{token}}” is not a valid predecessor entry. Write row numbers separated by semicolons, optionally with a dependency type (FS, SS, FF, SF) and lag, e.g. 2; 5+3; 6SS+2.
predecessorError.duplicate: Row {{row}} is listed twice among the predecessors.
predecessorError.phase: Row {{row}} is a phase. Linking to phases is not possible yet – link to its last task instead.
predecessorError.phaseSuccessor: A phase cannot have predecessors yet.
predecessorError.cycle: This link would create a loop {{path}} – the task would wait for itself.

schedule.noWorkingDays: The calendar has no working day, so no dates can be calculated. Adjust it under Calendar.

calendar.title: Project calendar
calendar.intro: Dates are calculated in working days only. Weekends, holidays and shutdowns are skipped.
calendar.projectStartHint: The first tasks start on the nearest working day from this date.
calendar.atLeastOneDay: At least one day of the week must be a working day.
calendar.holidaysHint: Days off by law of the selected country (for Germany only nationwide holidays, not those of individual states).
calendar.customIntro: E.g. company holiday or production shutdown. For a single day, enter the same date in both fields.
calendar.customMissingDates: Fill in both the from and to dates.
calendar.customEndBeforeStart: The “to” date cannot be before the “from” date.

sample.confirmReplace: Loading the sample project will replace the current plan. You can undo this with Undo (Ctrl+Z). Continue?

tasks.t6c: Interim manual production until trial run

lines.finalPayment: Final payment to the cell supplier (70 %)

intro.materials: Materials and parts with a unit price. On a task you will later enter only the quantity used – the price comes from here (a price change applies everywhere).
intro.costCategories: Categories used to sort costs (e.g. for the budget and charts). A category that is in use cannot be deleted.
intro.professions: Professions (roles) with an hourly rate – entered manually, or calculated from the wage, contributions, overhead and productive hours. A worker without their own rate takes the rate of their profession.
intro.workers: Specific people. Each belongs to a profession; they may have their own rate (manual or calculated), otherwise the profession rate applies.
intro.machines: Machines and equipment with an hourly or daily rate (rental, operation, depreciation). A rate calculation for machines will come later – for now the rate is entered manually.
intro.departments: Organisational units (departments, cost centres). A worker can be assigned to a department – analytics will then show costs and workload per department.

tracking.statusHint: The day for which planned work (PV), completed work (EV) and spending (AC) are calculated. Empty = today.

hint.eacNone: calculated after first costs and completed work

bac.name: BAC – Budget at Completion
bac.text: What the whole project should cost according to the saved baseline. It is the fixed point everything else is compared with.
bac.formula: BAC = sum of planned costs of all baseline items.

pv.name: PV – Planned Value
pv.text: How much work (in money) should be done by the status date according to the baseline.
pv.formula: PV = baseline planned costs from the start up to and including the status date.

ev.name: EV – Earned Value
ev.text: How much work is really done, valued at the planned price of that work. A task worth 10,000 that is 40 % done has EV 4,000 – no matter how much was actually spent.

ac.name: AC – Actual Cost
ac.text: What was really spent up to the status date. It is recorded on tasks in the Task detail panel (Actual costs section).
ac.formula: AC = sum of actual costs dated up to and including the status date.

spi.name: SPI – Schedule Performance Index
spi.text: Whether work progresses as planned. 1 = exactly on plan, below 1 = behind (0.8 = only 80 % of what should be done), above 1 = ahead.
spi.formula: SPI = EV / PV; variance SV = EV − PV (money).

cpi.name: CPI – Cost Performance Index
cpi.text: How much work we get for every unit of money spent. 1 = on budget, below 1 = more expensive (0.9 = only 0.90 worth of work per 1 spent), above 1 = cheaper.
cpi.formula: CPI = EV / AC; variance CV = EV − AC (money).

eac.name: EAC – Estimate at Completion
eac.text: What the project will finally cost if it keeps performing as so far (same CPI). ETC is what is still left to spend.
eac.formula: EAC = BAC / CPI; ETC = EAC − AC.

vac.name: VAC – Variance at Completion
vac.text: How much the estimated final cost differs from the plan. Negative = budget overrun, positive = saving.

learn.title: How to read Earned Value
learn.p1: Earned Value compares three amounts of money: what should be done (PV), what is done (EV) and what it cost (AC). All are calculated as of the status date.
learn.p2: You spot a delay by EV < PV (SPI below 1) and an overrun by AC > EV (CPI below 1). Both can happen at once – or mask each other, so look at both indices.
learn.p3: EV comes from the % complete you enter on tasks in the plan. The more honestly you enter it, the truer the picture.
learn.p4: When the plan changes substantially (an approved scope change), save a new baseline and select it for comparison. You can keep the old one for reference.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.intro: Short explanations of the terms the app works with. You will find the same explanations behind the ⓘ buttons throughout the app.

mindMap.name: Mind map
mindMap.text: A picture with the main topic (the project) in the middle and its parts and sub-parts branching out from it. It helps you think through what the project consists of, still without dates. You can then create a plan from the map: branches become phases, end nodes become tasks.

phase.name: Phase
phase.text: A group of related tasks, e.g. “Design and engineering”. Its start, finish, duration, costs and % complete are calculated from the items inside – you do not enter them. A phase can be collapsed and expanded.

milestone.name: Milestone
milestone.text: An important moment in the project with zero duration, e.g. signing a contract or handover. It is shown as a diamond in the chart. It may only have a one-off cost or material.

wbs.name: WBS (structure number)
wbs.text: Work Breakdown Structure – splitting the project into smaller parts. A number such as 2.3.1 tells where the item sits in the tree (first item in the third item of the second phase). The app numbers it automatically. Predecessors are written using the No. column, not WBS.

duration.name: Duration
duration.text: The number of working days a task takes. Weekends, holidays and shutdowns are not counted, so 5 days may span more than a week in the calendar. A milestone has duration 0.

workingDays.name: Working day and calendar
workingDays.text: A day when work is done on the project: by default Monday to Friday, without Czech public holidays and your own exceptions (shutdown, company holiday). Set it in the Calendar window.

dependency.name: Dependency (predecessor and successor)
dependency.text: Says that one task depends on another. The predecessor is the one being waited for, the successor is the one waiting. When the predecessor moves, the app recalculates the successors. In the Predecessors column, write the row number from the No. column, e.g. 3 or 3FS+2.

linkTypes.name: Dependency types FS, SS, FF, SF
linkTypes.text: FS (finish-to-start, default): the successor starts after the predecessor finishes. SS (start-to-start): starts no earlier than the predecessor starts. FF (finish-to-finish): finishes no earlier than the predecessor finishes. SF (start-to-finish): finishes no earlier than the working day before the predecessor starts.

lag.name: Lag and lead
lag.text: Extra working days between the predecessor and the successor. A positive number is a wait (3FS+2 = two days after row 3 finishes), a negative one is a lead – the successor overlaps the predecessor (3FS-2).

constraint.name: “Start no earlier than” constraint (📌)
constraint.text: A date before which the task will not start. It is created by dragging the bar or entering the start in the table. The actual start is the latest of: project start, dependencies, constraint. Click 📌 to remove the constraint.

criticalPath.name: Critical path
criticalPath.text: The chain of tasks the project finish directly depends on – they have no slack. If any of them is one day late, the project finishes one day later. The Critical path toggle highlights them in yellow.

slack.name: Slack (total and free)
slack.text: How many working days an item may be delayed. Total slack: without moving the project finish. Free slack: without moving any successor. An item with zero slack is critical.

resource.name: Resource
resource.text: What the project consumes: people (professions and workers), machines and material. Resources are created on the Resources screen and added to tasks as lines in the Task detail panel.

rate.name: Hourly rate
rate.text: How much one hour of a person’s or machine’s work costs. For people, the app calculates it from wage, contributions, overhead and productive hours (Calculation button); a manual rate overrides the calculation.

load.name: Load
load.text: How many hours per day a resource is planned compared to its capacity (h/day), in per cent. 100 % means fully loaded.

overload.name: Overload
overload.text: A day when a resource is planned for more hours than its capacity (load above 100 %). An absent worker has capacity 0. Dates do not change by themselves – move tasks or add people.

costLine.name: Cost line
costLine.text: One resource or item on a task: person, machine, material, one-off or recurring cost. A task’s cost is the sum of its lines, a phase’s cost the sum of everything inside.

costCategory.name: Cost category
costCategory.text: A type of expense, e.g. wages, material, services, investment. Overviews are grouped by category and limits can be set for them.

tags.name: Tags
tags.text: Free words on cost lines, e.g. “grant” or “external”. Used for filtering and grouping in the Costs and Analysis views.

costTimeline.name: Cost timeline
costTimeline.text: Costs spread over individual days according to task dates: work evenly over working days, material on the start day, a one-off cost on the chosen day. Shows when money will be needed.

budgetLimit.name: Budget limit
budgetLimit.text: The maximum amount the project or a category may cost. The app shows the spending in % and the day from which the cumulative costs would exceed the limit.

sCurve.name: S-curve
sCurve.text: A chart of cumulative costs over time. It rises slowly at the beginning and end of the project and quickly in the middle – hence the S shape. Shows how much will be spent by a given day.

cashFlow.name: Cash flow
cashFlow.text: How much money goes out in each period (week, month, quarter). Helps find the periods with the highest spending. Expenses only for now, no income.

pivot.name: Pivot table
pivot.text: A table that adds up numbers by the criteria you choose for rows and columns, e.g. costs by phase and month. Criteria are switched without writing formulas.

percentComplete.name: % complete
percentComplete.text: How much work on an item is done. Entered manually for a task, calculated for a phase (weighted by planned cost); a milestone is either done (100 %) or not (0 %). In the chart it is the darker fill of the bar from the left.

baseline.name: Baseline
baseline.text: A saved snapshot of the plan – dates and costs – usually on the day it is approved. The later plan and the actuals are compared to it. The Baseline toggle shows a grey shadow of the original dates under the bars.

statusDate.name: Status date
statusDate.text: The day for which the project status is evaluated (today if empty). Only actual cost entries up to and including this day are counted.

actualCost.name: Actual costs
actualCost.text: What was really paid for a task, entered as dated entries in the Task detail panel. The Tracking view compares them with the plan.

earnedValue.name: Earned Value
earnedValue.text: A method comparing three numbers: how much work should be done (PV), how much really is done (EV) and what it cost (AC). They reveal both delays and overspending. The individual indicators are explained below and on the tiles in the Tracking view.

check.title: Plan check
check.intro: The app went through the plan and found places where something is probably missing or does not add up. These are only warnings – they block nothing and change nothing. Each has a “How to fix” tip.
check.none: We found nothing suspicious in the plan. 👍
check.empty: The plan is empty so far – nothing to check.

kinds.leadBeforePredecessor: Dependency into the past: lead longer than the predecessor
kinds.notStarted: Dependency into the past: should have started but has not

items.budgetOverProject: The planned project costs exceed the limit by {{amount}}.
items.leadBeforePredecessor: “{{task}}” would start, according to the {{link}} dependency on “{{predecessor}}”, before the predecessor itself.
items.notStarted: “{{task}}” should have started on {{date}} but is 0 % complete.
items.notStartedMilestone: Milestone “{{task}}” was due on {{date}} but is not done.
items.zeroDuration: “{{task}}” has a duration of 0 working days.
items.noPredecessor: “{{task}}” has no predecessor, so it starts right at the project start.

fix.budgetOver: Reduce costs (fewer hours, a cheaper resource, less material), or, if agreed, raise the limit in the Costs view with the Budget limits button. The S-curve chart shows the day the limit is exceeded.
fix.overload: In the Load view, find the overloaded days and the tasks causing them. Then move a task (by dragging its bar or with a dependency), lower the % share, assign a different worker, or make the task longer. The app does not change dates because of overload by itself.
fix.leadBeforePredecessor: The lead (negative lag) is longer than the predecessor lasts, so the dependency makes no sense. Shorten the lead in the Predecessors column (e.g. 3FS-4 → 3FS-2), or choose another dependency type, such as SS (start-to-start).
fix.notStarted: If the work has started, enter the % complete (tick done for a milestone). If it has not, move the start to the real date – by dragging the bar or in the Start column. The successors move with it.
fix.zeroDuration: Enter the number of working days in the Duration column. If it is a moment without duration (signing, handover), change the type to Milestone.
fix.emptyPhase: Add tasks to the phase (select the phase and click Add task, or indent a task under it), or delete the phase if you do not need it.
fix.noPredecessor: In the Predecessors column, enter the row number (No. column) of the task it has to wait for. If it really should start at the project start, you can ignore the warning – or give it a fixed start 📌 by dragging its bar.
fix.noSuccessor: When nothing waits for a task, the plan cannot show what its delay would cause. Make it the predecessor of another task or of a final milestone (e.g. Handover). If nothing really waits for it, you can ignore the warning.

newProject.intro: Start with an empty plan, or pick a template from engineering and manufacturing. A template contains phases, tasks, dependencies, resources and a budget – just adapt it to your needs.

templates.automation: A robotic workcell from the feasibility study through tendering, manufacturing and installation to trial operation and handover.

templates.investment: Construction of a warehouse hall: from the investment proposal and financing through design documentation, the building permit and contractor selection to construction, final approval and start of operation.
templates.shutdown: A production shutdown for a press overhaul, part replacement and inspections: planning, ordering parts and building up stock, parallel work during the shutdown and a safe production restart.

ai.planPrompt:
You are an experienced project manager in an engineering and manufacturing company. Draft a schedule and a rough budget for the project described below. The result will be loaded by the MiRo project app, so it must follow the format exactly.

PROJECT BRIEF
Name: {{name}}
Start: {{start}}
Budget currency: {{currency}}
Description:
{{description}}

RULES
1. Split the project into 3–8 phases (kind "phase"). Every task (kind "task") and milestone (kind "milestone") belongs to a phase: field "parent" = the phase "id". Phases may contain sub-phases, at most 6 levels.
2. 15–60 items in total. Short, specific names in English.
3. "duration" is the number of WORKING days (integer). Milestones and phases have "duration": 0 (a phase's duration is calculated).
4. Dependencies ("dependsOn") only between tasks and milestones, never with a phase. Types: "FS" = starts after the predecessor finishes (default), "SS" = starts no earlier than the predecessor starts, "FF" = finishes no earlier than the predecessor finishes, "SF" = finishes no earlier than the predecessor starts. "lag" = delay in working days (negative = lead). Dependencies must not form a cycle.
5. Every task and milestone except the very first has at least one predecessor. Something follows every task and milestone except the last. The project ends with a milestone (handover).
6. Costs ("costs") are a rough estimate in {{currency}} excluding VAT. "amount" is a number without spaces or currency. "when": "start" / "end" = one-off at the start / end of the item, "perDay" / "perWeek" / "perMonth" = recurring for every working day / week / month of the item's duration. "category": "material", "labor", "services", "investment", "overhead" or "reserve". Estimate your own staff's work as a recurring cost in category "labor". A milestone may only have "start" or "end" costs. Include a reserve ("reserve").
7. "id" is short and unique (e.g. "F1", "T3", "M2").

RESPONSE FORMAT
Reply ONLY with a single JSON block, no other text, exactly in this shape (example):
{{example}}

risks.label: Find plan risks
risks.text: Review the plan and find the biggest risks (dates, dependencies, resources, budget). For each risk, suggest a specific measure.

shorten.label: Suggest how to finish sooner
shorten.text: Suggest how to shorten the project completion date (overlapping tasks, leads, more resources). For each suggestion, state how many working days the finish moves and what the risk is.

budget.label: Review the budget
budget.text: Review the project budget: are any usual costs missing, are some amounts unrealistic, and is the reserve sufficient? Answer specifically, item by item.

criticalPath.label: Explain the critical path
criticalPath.text: Explain to a student planning for the first time what the critical path is in this project, why it runs through exactly these tasks and what would happen if one of them were late.

status.label: Assess project status
status.text: Using the Earned Value indicators (SPI, CPI, EAC) and % complete, assess where the project stands and suggest what to do next. Explain it clearly, even for a layperson.

export.intro: A project from the MiRo project app (Gantt chart with a budget). Durations are in working days, amounts in {{currency}} excluding VAT. Column # is the row number; predecessors are written as row number and dependency type (e.g. 3FS+2).

The app prepares a description of the project (dates, budget, warnings) and a question. Copy the text and paste it into an AI chat such as ChatGPT or Claude. Nothing is sent automatically – the data leave your computer only when you paste them into the AI yourself.
